title: Runtime Regression: Causality Log for Flash Rework, Paged-KV Compaction, and Continuous Batching
content:
Summary:
This log captures an applied-ML investigation into a post-deploy regression observed after three coordinated runtime changes landed in the serving runtime:
  1) flash-attention rewrite (kernel reorder + fused matmul path),
  2) paged-KV compaction heuristic update (aggressive compaction at 75% occupancy), and
  3) continuous-batching allocator tweak (pack-first change for latency optimization).

Observed outward symptoms (production signals):
- Increase in tail latency for some short-context instruction workloads (p95 +18ms, p99 +38ms) starting 2026-04-10 03:00 UTC.
- Lowered token throughput on some L2 caches tests (tokens/sec down ~12% on smaller batch sizes).
- Small, reproducible semantic quality delta for the instruction-following prompt set used in model onboarding: ROUGE-L drop ~0.6–0.9 across prompts; hallucination flag rate +1.2 percentage points on a 500-prompt subset.

Incident timeline (high level):
- 2026-04-09: PRs merged for all three changes (linked above). Canary runs looked clean on a narrow prompt mix.
- 2026-04-10 02:30 UTC: Canary traffic expanded to 10%; automated evals on internal prompt sets start to show divergence at 05:00 UTC.
- 2026-04-10 07:00 UTC: Alerting fired for p99 latency; rollback not triggered automatically.
- 2026-04-11: Applied-ML triage begins; deeper evals launched across onboarding prompt sets.

Affected models & configs examined:
- open-llm-13b-v2 quantized (Q4*), hosted in Dedicated pool g4-like node.
- open-llm-7b instruction-tuned (float16).
- All runs used default KV page size 128, compaction threshold 0.75, continuous-batching enabled with pack-first heuristic.

Evaluation suite and prompt sets used for triage:
- prompt-instr-500: 500 short instruction-following prompts (single-turn), used for onboarding quality checks.
- summarization-100: longer-context (512–1024 tokens) summaries used to exercise KV cache behavior.
- code-gen-50: small code generation tasks that are latency-sensitive for early tokens.
- stress-seqlen: synthetic suite to exercise paging and eviction patterns.

Key diffs from regression evals (representative results):
- latency_deltas: median +6ms, p95 +18ms, p99 +38ms (most visible on prompt-instr-500).
- throughput: tokens/sec -12% for batch size 1–4; +4% for very large batches (>32).
- quality_metrics: prompt-instr-500 ROUGE-L -0.7 avg, exact-match-like metrics for few-shot QA -0.4 points, hallucination flag +1.2 pp.
- KV hit rate: global KV hit rate decreased from 91.3% -> 86.1% on summarization-100 runs (compaction appears correlated).

Reproduction notes (local + staging):
- Reproduced on a staging Dedicated stack with the same GPU drivers and CUDA 12.0.
- Repro procedure: serve model with new runtime, run prompt-instr-500 serially (no batching) and record latency + logits.
- When paged-KV compaction is toggled back to previous threshold (0.90), KV hit rate and ROUGE-L largely recover.
- When flash-attention rework is disabled, median latency slightly increases but tail latency drops; semantic quality differences disappear.
- Continuous-batching pack-first increases batch packing density; for short prompts it causes the first-token scheduling to wait longer in some micro schedules producing p99 spikes.

Root cause hypotheses and evidence:
1) Paged-KV compaction aggressiveness -> increased cache churn -> quality regressions
   - Evidence: immediate KV hit-rate drop when compaction threshold set to 0.75; quality metrics (ROUGE-L, hallucination) correlate with KV hit rate over the prompt set.
   - Mechanism: compaction moves pages more frequently and invalidates warm KV entries for short-context prompts that re-use prefix state.

2) Flash-attention reorder creates non-deterministic micro-timing for early-token compute paths -> tail latency spikes
   - Evidence: disabling flash rework lowers p99 while slightly raising median; profiling shows kernel launch overlap differences for small sequence lengths.
   - Mechanism: new fused path increases register pressure -> occasional kernel fallback to slower path if occupancy not optimal; fallback happens rarely but causes large tail.

3) Continuous-batching pack-first heuristic + KV compaction synergy -> batching delays + cache misses -> perceivable quality and latency impact on short workloads
   - Evidence: enabling pack-first with compaction at 0.75 produces the worst combined deltas; isolating either change reduces the effect.

Investigation artifacts and traces (high-level):
- Per-request trace ids: sample traces stored in S3 under s3://redwood-traces/regression-2026-04/ (see linked_artifacts for trace manifest).
- Kernel-level timeline captures: collected via perf tracing on staging GPUs (perf samples attached to PR 2713).
- Eval diffs: CSVs with per-prompt deltas uploaded to internal bucket (linked in Confluence page ENG-1142).

Immediate mitigations and rollback recommendations:
- Short term (0–24h): revert paged-KV compaction threshold to 0.90 on the affected Dedicated pools and roll back continuous-batching pack-first change for canary cohorts. This yields fastest quality/latency recovery in staging reproductions. Owner: SRE/Infra (Lucas Ortega).
- Medium term (24h–1w): revert flash-attention rework from canary to behind a runtime flag and add an occupancy-aware fallback explicit guard to avoid rare slower-path fallbacks. Owner: Serving Runtime team (Ethan Zhao).
- Instrumentation: add per-request KV hit annotations to the tracing pipeline, and add a small synthetic heartbeat suite that runs prompt-instr-50 at 1% of traffic to detect quality regressions earlier. Owner: Applied ML (Priya Nair, Maya Singh).

Proposed rollout plan after fixes:
1) Add a guarded canary: deploy compaction 0.75 + pack-first behind a feature flag for <1% traffic and run both automated evals and synthetic heartbeats for 48h.
2) If no regression, expand to 10% with continuous monitoring on KV hit rate, ROUGE-L on onboarding set, and p99 latency.
3) Gradual increase with automated rollback triggers if any metric crosses thresholds: p99 > baseline +25ms OR KV hit rate drops >3pp OR ROUGE-L drop >0.4.

Open questions and next investigations:
- Why does flash-attention fused path cause occasional kernel fallback only on some sequence-length distributions? Need micro-benchmarks by sequence-length and occupancy.
- Is there an alternative compaction policy that preserves page locality for small-context workloads (e.g., LRU-weighting per-request signature)?
- Can continuous-batching scheduler be augmented to prioritize first-token latency for low-length sessions without sacrificing throughput for large batches?

Action items (owners):
- Revert compaction threshold in Dedicated canaries (Lucas Ortega) — target: 2026-04-17 10:00 UTC.
- Feature-flag the flash-attention rework and add occupancy guard (Ethan Zhao) — target: 2026-04-20.
- Add KV-hit annotations and synthetic heartbeat checks to onboarding pipeline (Priya Nair, Maya Singh) — target: 2026-04-19.
- Create micro-bench harness for flash-attention occupancy by seq-len (Hannah Lee) — target: 2026-04-22.

Appendix (quick reproduction commands):
1) Start staging runtime with the current branch and a single model pool: ./deploy.sh --env staging --branch runtime/rework-2026
2) Run serial onboarding eval: python tools/run_eval.py --suite prompt-instr-500 --endpoint https://staging-infer.redwood.internal --collect-traces
3) Toggle paged-kv threshold (runtime flag): curl -X POST https://staging-admin.redwood.internal/runtime/config -d '{"kv_compaction_threshold": 0.9}'

Notes: This document is intended to be a living triage log for the applied-ML + serving-runtime investigation. I will update with micro-bench numbers and trace links as they are available.

Prepared by: Priya Nair (applied-ml)
Last update: 2026-04-17
